edges.mechanism: MK-7 supplies vitamin K for hepatic carboxylation of clotting factors, which directly antagonizes VKA effect. Its long half-life and accumulation make it more potent than K1.
edges.evidence: Volunteer dose-response study: 10-20 ug/day lowered INR in 40-60% of subjects, and 45 ug/day lowered INR by about 40%. PK comparison flags >=50 ug/day. The warfarin label lists vitamin K intake as a cause of reduced INR response.

edges.mechanism: True pharmacodynamic lowering of INR in VKA-treated people, not an assay artifact.
Natto is the richest dietary MK-7 source. It raises serum MK-7 and affects INR in VKA users.
edges.evidence: Reviews and observational MA; a low-MK-7 natto (46 ug/day) did not change INR in 10 warfarin patients.

edges.mechanism: DOAC anticoagulation does not depend on vitamin K, so no antagonism is expected. Switching off a VKA improves vitamin K status.
edges.evidence: Valkyrie RCT in HD AF patients: rivaroxaban plus MK-7 2000 ug thrice weekly; bleeding not different from rivaroxaban alone except fewer major bleeds than VKA.

edges.mechanism: May suppress gut menaquinone-producing bacteria. The warfarin label requires INR monitoring when starting or stopping antibiotics.
edges.evidence: IOM review of case reports, which are confounded; label guidance.

edges.mechanism: MK-7 modestly lowers FPG, HbA1c and HOMA-IR, so an additive effect is possible.
edges.evidence: RCT in T2D (360 ug/day): FPG ES -0.68, HbA1c ES -0.36. MAs show heterogeneous small effects. No interaction study.
RCT (n=77): combination improved BMD more than vitamin K2 alone. K2 form not specified.

edges.mechanism: Complementary bone-mineral actions: D raises osteocalcin expression and calcium absorption, and K carboxylates osteocalcin and MGP.
edges.evidence: K+D MA: total BMD SMD 0.316 and lower ucOC. AVADEC (720 ug MK-7 + D3) null for valve calcification. Baseline K status did not modify D3 effects.

edges.mechanism: Both forms add to total vitamin K, which matters for VKA users. K1 lowered dp-ucMGP more than K2 in dialysis.
edges.evidence: Review; dialysis MA (dp-ucMGP SMD -1.64 for K1 vs -0.56 for K2).

edges.mechanism: Overlapping vitamin K activity. MK-4 at nutritional doses is poorly bioavailable compared with MK-7, so stacking adds little status but still counts for VKA users.
High-dose alpha-tocopherol antagonizes vitamin K-dependent carboxylation.
edges.evidence: RCTs: 1000 IU/day raised PIVKA-II. IOM states vitamin E antagonism of vitamin K is established.

edges.mechanism: Often co-formulated. Adding Ca 500 mg + D3 10 ug to 90 ug K2 gave no added BMD benefit.
A fat/n-3 PUFA-containing food matrix may enhance MK-7 absorption.
edges.evidence: Small study: a multi-nutrient yogurt (including n-3 PUFA and fish oil) raised plasma MK-7 more than capsules; the effect was not isolated to n-3.

edges.mechanism: Functional vitamin K deficiency is common. MK-7 corrects biomarkers but not calcification, stiffness or mortality. One trial showed site-specific radius BMD loss.
edges.evidence: Multiple RCTs (RenaKvit, Trevasc-HDK, K4Kidneys) and MAs; moderate certainty of no benefit.

edges.mechanism: Deficiency is common. MK-7 may slow arterial stiffening.
edges.evidence: RCT n=40 (PWV -0.06 vs +0.27 m/s) and single-arm study.

edges.mechanism: Vitamin K is poorly absorbed in lipid malabsorption syndromes, so supplement response may be reduced.
Vitamin K lowers PIVKA-II, which can mask an elevated HCC marker. The marker should be measured without vitamin K administration.
edges.evidence: HCC cohort studies (mostly MK-4/mixed vitamin K) plus MK-7 RCTs showing PIVKA-II decreases.

edges.mechanism: Supplementation lowers inactive MGP and undercarboxylated osteocalcin. These are intake/status markers, not outcomes.
CC carriers had higher ucOC after K2+/-D3. This is a possible attenuated carboxylation response.
